chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Aban ibn Taghlub. He said:

Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: Verily, when the believer has a nightmare, his sins are forgiven. And verily, when he is afflicted in his body, his sins are forgiven.

key_terms.مَنَام: Sleep, place of sleep; in context: during the dream/nightmare state
key_terms.يُمْتَهَن: To be tested, tried, or afflicted — specifically bodily illness
key_terms.يُهَوَّلُ: To be terrified, to experience nightmare/horror in sleep

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about nightmares and illness as means of forgiveness for believers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that God in His mercy uses two forms of tribulation — nightmares and bodily illness — as means of expiation for a believer's sins. This hadith reflects the Shia theological understanding that suffering in this world can purify the soul, and that divine mercy encompasses even the unconscious experiences of the faithful. The early audience would have understood this as a profound consolation, affirming that hardships are not punishments but opportunities for divine forgiveness.
